name: FX fix momentum/reversal around WMR 4pm London, Tokyo and ECB/Frankfurt fixes
source_url: https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.13306 (Krohn, Mueller, Whelan, Journal of Finance 2024); working paper https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2021/10/staff-working-paper-2021-48/ ; Michelberger & Witte https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.07778 ; Pragma summary https://www.euromoney.com/article/27bjsstsqxhkmh0ydxfsr/foreign-exchange/trading-is-predictable-during-wm-4pm-fix-says-pragma/
author_year: Krohn, Mueller & Whelan (2024 JF; 2021 WP); Marsh, Panagiotou & Payne (WMR 4pm study); Michelberger & Witte (2015, rev. 2016); Pragma research (2015-2016)
instrument: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY (Maven MT5 symbol mapping: same names; availability in Maven not verified [uncertain])
timeframe: 1-minute bars for fix-window microstructure; 5-minute window for WMR 4pm; hourly or intraday for pre/post-fix returns [uncertain]
entry_rule: Not fully specified in sources. Documented pattern: USD rises into the fix and falls after it (Krohn et al.), and in the WMR 4pm 5-minute window the first-minute move is followed by momentum then reversion (Pragma). Candidate fade rule to be pre-registered: after the fix time, take the position against the direction of the move during the pre-fix window; exact start/end minutes [uncertain].
exit_rule: Not reported in sources. Candidate: time exit after a fixed number of minutes after the fix (for example 30 to 60 minutes) [uncertain].
stop_rule: Not reported in sources. Stop distance and ATR multiple [uncertain].
holding_time: Minutes to about one hour for the reversal leg; not reported in sources [uncertain].
trades_per_year: Up to about 250 per year per fix per pair if traded daily on weekdays (derived, not sourced) [uncertain]
overnight_weekend: No for the London 4pm WMR and ECB fix windows; Tokyo fix is within the Asian session. Krohn et al. study around-the-clock returns, so the reversal can span session boundaries [uncertain]
signal_window_definition: Fix times assumed from general knowledge, not verified against sources: WMR London 16:00 London local (5-minute window 15:55-16:00 widened in 2015); Tokyo fix 09:55 Tokyo; ECB 14:15 CET/CEST. DST: Krohn et al. include a 'Daylight Savings Time Test' section but the handling rule was not extracted [uncertain]. Overnight return inclusion: as in Krohn et al. around-the-clock design [uncertain]
sample_period: Krohn et al.: about 21 years (exact dates not extracted) [uncertain]; Pragma: 15 Feb 2015 to 31 Dec 2015 (normal, month-end and quarter-end days)
out_of_sample: Not reported in the sources that were readable. Pragma notes that since the February 2016 WMR methodology change, momentum on ordinary days weakened while reversion remained roughly as strong; this is a descriptive post-change check, not a pre-registered out-of-sample test [uncertain]
cost_assumption: Not reported in the readable sources. Pragma sells execution algorithms and its research is not a trading backtest [uncertain]
reported_metrics: Pragma: quarter-end momentum about 10 bp then reversion about 6 bp; month-end momentum about 6 bp then reversion about 4 bp (conditioned on first-minute move). Krohn et al. working paper: long-all-G9 portfolio daily average swing of about 2 bp (sentence truncated in search snippet) [uncertain]. Krohn et al. JF: daily swings above USD 1 billion in spot volume; Sharpe, expectancy and win rate not reported. Marsh-Panagiotou-Payne: small price reversal in the minute after 4pm fix (magnitude not extracted) [uncertain]
third_party_replication: Partial. Michelberger & Witte (arXiv, independent authors) study WM/Reuters 4pm microstructure and report higher volatility and movement size around 4pm, without numbers in the abstract. Marsh, Panagiotou & Payne report a 1-minute reversal. Pragma is an industry source, not an independent academic test
evidence_grade: Peer-reviewed (Krohn, Mueller & Whelan, Journal of Finance 2024) for the broad FX fix reversal; working paper and arXiv for microstructure; practitioner summary (Pragma) for the 4pm momentum-reversal magnitudes
decay_status: Partially documented. Pragma: ordinary-day momentum weakened after the Feb 2016 WMR methodology change, reversion persisted; quarter- and month-end effects strongest. Krohn et al. report persistent reversals over 21 years [uncertain for post-2020 persistence]
regime_split: Yes, qualitative: Pragma splits pre/post Feb 2016 methodology change; Krohn et al. include a DST test and a section on changing trading patterns around the London fix. Numeric split not extracted [uncertain]
data_source_requirement: 1-minute or tick data for EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY with exact time-zone timestamps and DST handling; no options, VIX, or external fix prices needed if the fix is defined by clock time. Maven MT5 history depth and tick availability not verified [uncertain]
min_lot_fit_5k10k: Stop not defined. Illustration: EURUSD 0.01 lot, pip value about USD 0.10; a 20-pip stop risks about USD 2 = 0.04% of USD 5,000 or 0.02% of USD 10,000. Final percentage depends on the stop rule [uncertain]
fn_rule_fit: FundedNext rules not verified in this session [uncertain]. Fix windows are scheduled, not news, but the ECB fix can coincide with ECB decision days; the 5-minute window must be checked against the +/-5 minute news rule [uncertain]. Low-frequency single entry per fix is not HFT, grid, or tick scalping by construction
bot_policy_compliance: Fully rule-based and time-triggered; implementable as an EA with no messaging link needed. FundedNext bot policy text not verified in this session [uncertain]
event_overlap: London 16:00 fix overlaps with the US 11:00 ET hour and with month-end and quarter-end flows (which carry the strongest effect). ECB 14:15 CET fix overlaps with ECB decision days. Scheduled macro releases at 08:30 and 10:00 ET are outside the window in most cases [uncertain]
overlap_with_existing: Low to moderate. Donchian XAU 1H and Sweep US100 are at different instruments and times; EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY are not currently in the live set. Overlap estimate is qualitative [uncertain]
rejected_catalog_hit: Not checked. Run: python -m intraday.elenenler --kontrol fix (in the main session) [uncertain]
base_rate_check: Not computed. The claimed reversal is a documented directional pattern, so a 50% base-rate comparison and the 2 to 6 bp magnitude relative to typical EURUSD spread (about 1 pip = 1 bp) must be tested on Maven-measured spread [uncertain]
pitfall_risk: High. (1) Post-hoc window choice: Pragma's window was widened in 2015, so windows must be pre-registered; (2) overlapping legs across three fixes and multiple pairs inflate n; (3) magnitudes of about 2 to 6 bp are close to round-trip spread cost; (4) effect weakened after the 2016 methodology change; (5) practitioner source has commercial interest
